paras: You opened an AI chat, typed in a task from your real week, and got back a paragraph that sounded like a brochure. Maybe you tried it twice. Then you went back to doing the task by hand and decided the people raving about AI were exaggerating.

I spent most of a decade running performance marketing, and I have watched smart, busy people do the same. The tool they tried was good, but the request they gave it was thin, so the answer was thin, and most of them had never been shown how to direct it.

Two professionals can sit in front of the same AI tool with the same task. One gets a generic draft to fix. The other gets a near-final email. The gap between them is a skill, and this page shows you how to build it.
That is why I wrote The Artificial Advantage, and it is why I put this page together.

data.heading: What directing looks like
paras: Here is an invented example, so you can see the difference before you decide anything.
A thin request: Write an email about the delay.

A directed request: You are an operations manager at a mid-sized furniture company. Write a 120-word email to a customer whose sofa is two weeks late. Apologise once, give the new delivery date of November 14, offer free white-glove delivery, and keep the tone warm and direct.
The second request gives the AI a role, a task and the limits to work within. The book calls this the Role, Task, Constraint brief, and it is one of the tools you will learn.

data.heading: Who is writing to you
paras: My name is Elvin Peters. For three years I worked at goeasy, a Canadian lender with two regulated brands, easyfinancial and easyhome, where I ran the paid media myself. The budget was about $1.5M a month, more than $50M in all. Every campaign had to clear a compliance review before it went live, so I learned to be precise about what I asked for and careful about what I accepted.
After that I advised large advertisers at an ad tech company. In 2026 I became a founder, writing books and building with AI full time.

data.heading: What the book gives you
paras: The Artificial Advantage is fifteen chapters of method, built around a system called CLEAR: Choose your tools, Lead with clear direction, Evolve your outputs, Audit for accuracy, and Repeat to build a practice. You will learn:
How to brief AI with the Role, Task, Constraint framework, so the first answer is close to what you meant.
How to fix a weak answer with the Diagnostic Ladder, which traces a bad result to its cause.
How to check an answer before your name goes on it, with the Two-Step Verification Method.
How to turn a task you have mastered into a template, so next week takes a fraction of the effort.
What to do in your first week: pick one task you do regularly that feels tedious, and use AI on it.
It also holds 12 before-and-after prompt pairs, a Professional Prompt Library, ten common failures with the fix for each, and a 3-Month AI Practice Plan that turns the method into a habit.

The ebook alone is on Amazon at $9.99, and you are welcome to buy it there. This page is for readers who want the method and the files the same day. The box below is what this order includes, at the price the store is charging now.

data.heading: The 7-Day AI Workbook
paras: One stage of the CLEAR system each day, for seven days, using one real task of your own. On Day 2 you run the task the way you do today and save the result. On Day 7 you run the full loop again and compare. You finish with a before and an after, and a template you keep.
Prices are in US dollars.

items.q: Do I need a paid AI plan?
items.a: No. The book teaches skills that carry across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot. You can start on a free plan.

The book was written for professionals who tried AI and shrugged, and for people whose company just told them to use it. If you already use AI daily, the Diagnostic Ladder and the verification method are the chapters most likely to help.
The ebook, the Toolkit that comes with the book, the 7-Day AI Workbook, and the Companion Library. The price box on this page is the live list from the store.

I'll be recommending this to all of my coworkers who have been struggling with AI and prompting.
